info.title: Sessionboard Public API
info.description: REST API for managing sessions, speakers, contacts, sponsors, exhibitors, and event data on the Sessionboard platform.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Manage events on the platform.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Search and retrieve sessions within an event.

tags.name: Session Writes
tags.description: Create, update, delete, and restore sessions. Requires the `write:sessions` scope.

tags.name: Contact Writes
tags.description: Create, update, delete, and restore contacts. Requires the `write:contacts` scope.

tags.name: Exhibitor Writes
tags.description: Create, update, delete, and restore exhibitors. Requires the `write:exhibitors` scope.

tags.name: Sponsor Writes
tags.description: Create, update, delete, and restore sponsors. Requires the `write:sponsors` scope.

tags.name: Field Writes
tags.description: Create, update, and delete custom fields. Requires the `write:fields` scope.

tags.name: Speakers
tags.description: Search and retrieve speakers within an event.

tags.name: Participants
tags.description:
Search and retrieve every contact holding a session role on an event —
speakers, chairpersons, moderators and custom roles — with the roles
each one holds, and list the event's participant roles.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: Search and retrieve contacts at the organization or event level.

tags.name: Sponsors
tags.description: Search and retrieve sponsors within an event.

tags.name: Exhibitors
tags.description: Search and retrieve exhibitors within an event.

tags.name: Event Settings
tags.description: Retrieve event configuration such as fields, tags, tracks, rooms, formats, levels, languages, and session statuses.

tags.name: GDPR
tags.description: Manage GDPR data access and erasure requests.

tags.name: Insights
tags.description: Query event data using SbQL, generate queries with AI, and manage dashboards.

tags.name: Ask
tags.description: Ask a natural-language question about one event and get a cited answer. Requires the `read:ask` scope, granted explicitly.

tags.name: Sharing
tags.description: A webinar's sharing pieces, for your own tools and AI assistants — email signatures for your team, share cards, speakers' personal links and a draft kit of posts for your team. Reads need `read:events`, writes `write:marketing`. Webinars only. Sending email signatures from an AI assistant waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`).

tags.name: Event Emails
tags.description: An in-person event's or webinar's lifecycle emails (confirmation, reminders, replay) for your own tools and AI assistants. Reads need `read:events`. Designs an assistant proposes wait for a person to accept them in Sessionboard.

tags.name: Metadata Writes
tags.description: Create, update, and delete session metadata (rooms, tracks, tags, formats, levels, languages, statuses). Requires the `write:metadata` scope.

tags.name: Agenda Planning
tags.description: Manage agenda drafts, draft sessions, scheduling rules, and evaluation personas. Requires the `write:events` scope.

tags.name: Dashboards & Widgets
tags.description: Create, read, update, and delete dashboards and widgets at the event or organization level. Requires `write:events` scope for writes.

tags.name: Reports & Queries
tags.description: Create, read, update, delete, and run saved SbQL queries/reports at the event or organization level. Requires `write:events` scope for writes.

tags.name: Transcriptions
tags.description: Transcript text on sessions — fragments, summaries, insights, and translations. Requires `read:transcriptions` / `write:transcriptions` scopes.

tags.name: Session Recordings
tags.description: Session audio files for recording archives (live capture or imported audio). Requires `read:transcriptions` / `write:transcriptions` scopes.

tags.name: Media
tags.description: Upload video or audio files for automatic transcription. Requires `read:media` / `write:media` scopes.

tags.name: Session Files
tags.description:
Documents attached to sessions (PDFs, PowerPoint, Word, images, and similar).
Simple upload: `POST .../files/upload` (multipart, max 50 MB).
Direct-to-storage: create → PUT → complete (max 500 MB).
Requires `read:sessions` / `write:sessions` scopes.
See the [Uploading session files](/guides/uploading-session-files) guide.

tags.name: OAuth
tags.description: OAuth 2.1 endpoints for AI client authorization (Claude, ChatGPT). Mounted at `/oauth/` (not `/v1/`).

tags.name: Products
tags.description:
Which Sessionboard products your organization has: Platform, Sessions, CRM,
Awards, Learning and Marketing, each with whether it is owned and how
(a self-serve plan, or your Platform contract). Any `read:*` scope is enough.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
Your team's to-dos in Sessionboard Platform: a title, an assignee, a due
date with an optional time, a reminder, and the records each task is
about (contacts, sessions, sponsors, exhibitors, groups). Reads need
`read:tasks`, writes `write:tasks`. An organization on a self-serve
Sessionboard product gets `403 TASKS_PLATFORM_ONLY`. See the
[Tasks guide](/guides/tasks).

tags.name: Log Export
tags.description:
Pull your organization's API request, security and audit logs into a SIEM
such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel or Elastic. Requires a dedicated API token
with the `read:audit_logs` scope, which can call nothing else.
See the [Exporting logs to a SIEM](/guides/exporting-logs-to-a-siem) guide.

tags.name: Awards
tags.description: Read and manage Awards programs and their categories, rounds, promo codes, submissions and reviews. Organization-level: paths start at `/v1/organization/{orgId}/awards`. Requires `read:awards` / `write:awards` scopes.

tags.name: Learning
tags.description:
Turn Media-section videos (webinars, recordings, uploads, clips) into a course: draft it from
videos, review and edit the draft, then publish it and assign it. Organization-level: paths
start at `/v1/organization/{orgId}/learning`, and the same operations are served under
`/v1/learning` with the organization taken from the token. Requires the preview scopes
`read:learning` / `write:learning`, which a token or OAuth client gets only when they are
named explicitly (not by default, and not listed in `scopes_supported`). The organization
must have Learning turned on, and the token's user needs the Lessons permissions.

get.description:
Returns events accessible to the authenticated API key.

Results are paginated: `page` (1–999, default 1) and `pageSize`
(1–100, default 25) are honored, and the response wraps events in
the standard `{ results, pagination }` envelope. Events are ordered
oldest-first (`created_at` ascending, ties broken by `id`), so pages
are stable across requests.

By default each event is `id`, `name`, `timezone`, `starts_at`,
`ends_at`, and `features`. Pass `expand` to attach extra collections.

`expand=custom_fields` includes org-defined event custom field values
(`CustomFieldValue[]`). An event with no values returns `[]`.
Datetime custom field values are ISO 8601 in the event's local time
with its UTC offset (for example `2026-08-15T09:00:00-03:00`); when
the event has no valid timezone the raw UTC instant is returned
(`2026-08-15T12:00:00.000Z`). Date-only (`date`) fields serialize
as `M-DD-YYYY`: month without a leading zero, day with one, four-digit
year (for example `9-22-2026` for 22 September 2026, `3-04-2026` for
4 March 2026). This is not ISO 8601; parse it with that exact pattern.

`expand=integration_mappings` includes conference connector mappings
(`EventIntegrationMapping[]`) from `Integration_Event_Mapping_Union`
(Cvent, Grip, Swoogo, Swapcard, ASP, Stova, Bizzabo, Gleanin,
ExpoPlatform, ON24). `source` is the union key (underscores, e.g.
`expo_platform`). LiveBuzz / apps-engine campaign IDs are **not**
included in this expand.

Repeat the query param or comma-separate values:
`?expand=custom_fields&expand=integration_mappings`

post.description:
Search and filter sessions within an event. Supports pagination,
sorting, filtering by status, date ranges, and session categorization
(`trackIds`, `tagIds`, `levelIds`, `formatIds`, `languageIds`), and
expanding related data.

Each categorization filter needs at least one ID. An empty array is
rejected with a 400 naming the field — to apply no filter at all, omit
the property rather than sending `[]`.

`sort` uses nested keys — each sortable field is an object with a
`sort` direction, for example `{"sort": {"startsAt": {"sort": "asc"}}}`.
There is no flat `{"order": "...", "sort": "..."}` form. Sessions with
a null `starts_at` always sort last when sorting by `startsAt`,
regardless of direction.

Every session includes `is_abstract` and `composition_status`. Pass
`filters.isAbstract` to return only abstract submissions or only
program sessions. By default, sessions linked as composition sources
are excluded; pass `expand=linked_sources` to include them. Pass
`expand=composition` for full target/source details.

Each session in the response includes a `subsessions` array. By
default each subsession is returned in a minimal shape (`Subsession`).
Pass `expand=subsession_details` in the request body to receive full
parent-shape parity (`SubsessionDetailed`) on every subsession —
including `status`, `custom_status`, `custom_fields`, `chairpersons`,
`moderators`, `sponsors`, `exhibitors`, `tags`, `language`, `track`,
`level`, `room`, etc.

Each subsession inherits the parent session's `is_abstract`,
`composition_status`, and optional `composition` graph (when
`expand=composition` is set).

Nested `language`, `track`, `level`, `format`, and `room` objects on
each session include the field sets documented on the `Session` schema.
Unassigned metadata is returned as `{}`.

Paginated search responses return matching sessions under `results`
(not `data`), alongside a `pagination` object.

sortByStartTime.summary: Sort by session start time (nested sort syntax)
sortByStartTime.description:
Sort keys are nested objects — `{"startsAt": {"sort": "asc"}}`.
Sessions with a null `starts_at` always sort last, regardless
of direction.

filterByCategorization.description:
IDs within one filter match with OR; separate filters combine
with AND.

get.description:
Paginated list of top-level sessions via the CRUD proxy. Returns nested
`language`, `track`, `level`, `format`, and `room` metadata using the same
field sets documented on the `Session` schema (`null` when unassigned).
Also includes `is_abstract` and `composition_status`.

Query params: `is_abstract` (`true`/`false`), `expand=linked_sources`,
`expand=composition`, plus standard pagination and filters.

Session categorization filters use snake_case query params on this
endpoint: `track_id`/`track_ids`, `tag_id`/`tag_ids`,
`level_id`/`level_ids`, `format_id`/`format_ids`,
`language_id`/`language_ids`. Plural params take comma-separated UUIDs
(OR within a filter; separate filters combine with AND).

Every value passed to these filters must be a UUID. A non-UUID value
returns `400` with error code `VALIDATION_ERROR` and a message naming
the offending parameter, for example
`track_id must be a UUID (received "nope")`.

parameters.name: is_abstract
parameters.description: Filter to abstract submissions or program sessions.

parameters.name: track_id
parameters.description: Filter by a single track UUID.

parameters.name: track_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated track UUIDs (OR). Repeat `track_id` for the same effect.

400.description:
A categorization filter param (`track_id`/`track_ids`,
`level_id`/`level_ids`, `format_id`/`format_ids`,
`language_id`/`language_ids`, `tag_id`/`tag_ids`) carried a
non-UUID value. The message names the offending parameter.

post.description:
Returns a lightweight list of session statuses, including deleted
sessions. Supports filtering by `deletedAt` in addition to standard
filters.

Also accepts the five session categorization filters (`trackIds`,
`tagIds`, `levelIds`, `formatIds`, `languageIds`). IDs within one
filter match with OR; separate filters combine with AND. The filters
are evaluated against the **top-level (root) session**: a subsession
row matches when its parent carries the filtered attribute, so a
matching parent and the flat rows of its `subsessions` array stay
consistent. Unlike other session searches, a **deleted** root session
still satisfies a categorization filter — surfacing deleted sessions
is this endpoint's purpose, and filtering must not hide them.

Each categorization filter needs at least one ID. An empty array is
rejected with a 400 naming the field — to apply no filter at all, omit
the property rather than sending `[]`.

Parent rows additionally include a `subsessions` array with the same
minimal status-focused shape for each child subsession
(`SubsessionStatus`). Subsession rows that appear in the flat
results continue to surface with their own row (for back-compat) and
carry an empty `subsessions` array.

trackIds.description: Match sessions in any of these tracks (OR). Combined with other filters using AND. Evaluated against the top-level session; a deleted root still matches. Send at least one ID — an empty array is rejected with a 400; to apply no track filter, omit the property.

tagIds.description: Match sessions tagged with any of these tag IDs (OR). Send at least one ID — an empty array is rejected with a 400.

sort.description:
Nested sort keys — the same shape as other search endpoints
(`{"createdAt": {"sort": "desc"}}`), not a flat
`{"order": "createdAt", "sort": "desc"}` pair.

When sorting by `deletedAt`, deleted sessions sort before
never-deleted ones (whose `deleted_at` is null) in both
directions.

recentlyDeletedFirst.summary: Sort by deletion time (nested sort syntax)

declinedInTrack.summary: Declined sessions in a track (categorization filter)
declinedInTrack.description:
IDs within one filter match with OR; separate filters combine
with AND. Filters match the top-level session, so subsession
rows match via their parent — and a deleted root session
still matches.

get.description:
Retrieve a single session by ID, optionally expanding related data.

Every session includes `is_abstract` and `composition_status`. Pass
`expand=composition` for full linked target and source details.

Accepts both parent session UUIDs and subsession UUIDs. When called
with a subsession UUID, the response is a full session-shaped DTO
for that subsession (with `parent_session_friendly_id` /
`parent_session_friendly_id_raw` keys and no nested `subsessions`
array). Subsessions inherit the parent session's `is_abstract`,
`composition_status`, and optional `composition` graph (when
`expand=composition` is set) — subsessions cannot participate in
composition directly.

This means callers can iterate `parent.subsessions[]` and then call
this endpoint with each subsession id to retrieve the same shape
as a parent session.

Pass `expand=subsession_details` to receive the full
`SubsessionDetailed` shape on every entry of `parent.subsessions[]`;
the flag has no effect at the top level — the top-level response
always returns the full shape regardless of whether the requested
id is a parent or a subsession.

put.description: Update an existing session. Requires the `write:sessions` scope. Send `updated_at` from the last-fetched session for optimistic concurrency control.

updated_at.description: Required for optimistic concurrency control. Send the `updated_at` value from the last-fetched session.

custom_fields.description:
Custom field values keyed by field internal name.

For `number`, `currency`, and `percent` fields, an empty
string (`""`) clears the stored value — identical to
sending `null`. `0` and `"0"` store an actual zero.

For `checkbox` fields, send boolean `true` or `false`.
On read, a checked box serializes as the string `"Yes"`, an
explicitly unchecked one as `"No"`, and a box that was never
set as `null`.

Fields owned by an integration (for example
`swoogo_session_id`, `cvent_session_id`,
`visit_session_id`) are hydrated by the connector and
reject writes with `400` `FIELD_READ_ONLY`, naming the
field in `details.field`. Omit them from `custom_fields`.

translated_fields.description:
Language variants to write using the same shape returned on reads.
Omit this key on update to leave existing translations unchanged.

409.description: Stale update — session modified since last fetch

delete.description: Soft-delete a session. Can be restored with the restore endpoint. Requires the `write:sessions` scope.

put.description: Update custom field values on a session without touching other session properties. Requires the `write:sessions` scope.

values.description:
Field values to write. Unlike the session `PUT`, this
endpoint takes an array of entries rather than a
`custom_fields` object, and each entry may carry its own
`language` — so this is the endpoint to use for writing a
language variant of a single field. An empty or missing
array returns `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Value formatting per type matches `custom_fields`
elsewhere: an empty string (`""`) clears a `number`,
`currency`, or `percent` field; `checkbox` takes boolean
`true` / `false`; `datetime` takes an ISO 8601 string.

Fields owned by an integration (for example
`swoogo_session_id`, `cvent_session_id`,
`visit_session_id`) are hydrated by the connector and
reject writes with `400` `FIELD_READ_ONLY`, naming the
field in `details.field`.

internal_name.description: The field's internal name, as listed by `GET /v1/event/{eventId}/fields`.

value.description: The value to store. `null` clears it.

language.description: Optional locale for a language variant (for example `es_ES`). Must be one of the event's enabled locales. Omit it to write the event default.

variant.summary: Write a Spanish variant of one field

200.description:
Custom fields updated. The response echoes the fields that were
written rather than the whole session — refetch with
`GET /v1/event/{eventId}/sessions/{sessionId}` if you need the
full record.

language.description: Present only when the request specified a language.

400.description: Validation error — `values` missing or empty, an unknown field (`UNKNOWN_FIELD`), a type mismatch (`TYPE_MISMATCH`), or an integration-owned field (`FIELD_READ_ONLY`).

post.description:
Search and filter speakers within an event. Supports the session
categorization filters (`trackIds`, `tagIds`, `levelIds`, `formatIds`,
`languageIds`) to match speakers by the sessions they are assigned to.
`sort` uses the same nested shape as other search endpoints
(`{"createdAt": {"sort": "desc"}}`).

Categorization filters are evaluated against the **top-level
session**, matching session search semantics: a speaker assigned to a
subsession matches when the subsession's parent (root) session
satisfies the filter — a subsession's own categorization values are
not consulted.

Each categorization filter needs at least one ID. An empty array is
rejected with a 400 naming the field — to apply no filter at all, omit
the property rather than sending `[]`.

Only a session's **speakers** are matched. A contact attached to a
matching session as a chairperson, moderator or other participant is
not returned by this endpoint — with or without a filter. The session
object from `POST /v1/event/{eventId}/sessions` exposes four separate
participant arrays (`speakers`, `chairpersons`, `moderators`,
`participants`) and they are not interchangeable here: reconciling
"speakers on track X" against a session search must compare against
the `speakers` array alone, or the counts will not agree. The same
contact can appear under different roles on different sessions, so a
contact present in the unfiltered speaker list may still be absent
from a filtered one when its attachment to the matching session is a
non-speaker role.

To retrieve every participant regardless of role — chairpersons,
moderators and custom roles included, each with the roles it holds —
use `POST /v1/event/{eventId}/participants`. It accepts the same
filters and returns the same contact fields plus a `roles` array.

get.description: Retrieve a single speaker by contact ID.

post.description:
Search every contact assigned to at least one session on the event in
**any** participant role — the standard roles (speaker, chairperson,
moderator) and any custom role configured for the event (Panelist,
Coach, Author, …). This is the superset of
`POST /v1/event/{eventId}/speakers`, which matches speakers only.

Each contact is returned **once**, however many sessions or roles it
holds, with a `roles` array listing every role it has on the event and
the session ids where it holds each one. Every other field is the same
`Contact` shape `POST /speakers` returns, in the same order, with
`roles` appended last. `roles` always describes the contact's full
set of roles on the event — it is not narrowed by the request filters,
so a search filtered to the Moderator role still shows that a result is
also a Speaker elsewhere on the program.

**Filters.** Every Search Speakers filter is accepted and behaves the
same: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `status` (the *session's* status),
`trackIds`, `levelIds`, `formatIds`, `languageIds`, `tagIds`, plus
`sort` and `expand`. Categorization filters are evaluated against the
**top-level session**, so a participant on a subsession matches when
the subsession's parent satisfies the filter. Each array filter needs
at least one id — `[]` is a `400` naming the field; omit the property
to apply no filter.

Three filters are specific to this endpoint:

- `roleIds` — return only participants holding **at least one** of the
  given roles, standard or custom. Get the ids from
  `GET /v1/event/{eventId}/participant-roles`.
- `roleSlugs` — the same, by role slug (`speaker`, `chairperson`,
  `moderator`, or a custom role's slug). Use this to get every speaker
  without resolving ids per event, or on older events where roles have
  `roleId: null`.
- `email` — exact, case-insensitive match on the contact's email. An
  unknown address returns an empty `results` array with
  `totalResults: 0`, not an error. For a single-record lookup that
  answers `404` instead, use `GET /v1/event/{eventId}/participants?email=`.

**Roles on older events.** Roles are stored per event. An event that
has never been opened in the Sessions editor may not have its standard
roles created yet; its participants are still returned, but a
standard role on such an event has `roleId: null` (with `roleName`,
`slug` and `coreRole` filled in) and cannot be matched by `roleIds`
until the roles exist — filter by `roleSlugs` instead.
`GET .../participant-roles` returns an empty list for such an event.

byRole.summary: Everyone holding the Moderator or a custom role

400.description: Validation error — an empty filter array, a non-UUID in `roleIds`, or an out-of-range `page` / `pageSize`.

get.description:
Look up one participant by email address. The match is exact and
case-insensitive. Returns the participant, or `404` when no contact
with that address holds a session role on the event.

Search on this API is a `POST`, so a `GET` on the collection path is
free for the lookup — no `/by-email` sub-path is needed. `email` is
required; a bare `GET /participants` is a `400`, not an unpaginated
list.

Contacts are not unique by email. If more than one contact on the
event shares the address, the earliest-created one is returned; use
`POST /v1/event/{eventId}/participants` with the `email` filter to see
them all.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The contact's email address. Matched exactly, ignoring case.

404.description: Event not found, or no participant with that email on the event.

get.description:
Retrieve a single participant by contact ID, with the `roles` it holds
on the event. `404` when the contact is not on the event, or is on the
event but holds no session role — a contact returned by
`GET /v1/event/{eventId}/contacts/{contactId}` is not necessarily a
participant.

404.description: Participant not found on this event

get.description:
The event's participant roles — the three standard roles (Speaker,
Chairperson, Moderator) and every custom role configured for the
event — with the ids to use in the `roleIds` filter of
`POST /v1/event/{eventId}/participants`. Ordered as the Sessions
settings page shows them. Deleted roles are not returned.

`is_custom` is `true` for roles the organizer added. `core_role` is
the standard category a custom role maps to (`speaker`,
`chairperson` or `moderator`); it decides which legacy array the
role's participants appear in on `POST /v1/event/{eventId}/sessions`,
and is not a display label — use `name`.

An event that has never been opened in the Sessions editor may have no
roles yet and answers with an empty `results` array. Its participants
are still returned by `POST .../participants`, with `roleId: null` on
their standard roles until the roles are created.

get.description: Retrieve a single sponsor by ID.

404.description: No sponsor with this id on this event. A record that exists but does not hold the sponsor role — a contact, or a group linked only as the other role — is also a `404` here; look it up on the endpoint for the role it holds.

updated_at.description: Optional optimistic concurrency control. Send the `updated_at` value from the last-fetched sponsor.

name.description: New sponsor name. Must be a non-empty string when present — an explicit empty string returns `400`. Omit the key to leave the name unchanged.

custom_fields.description:
Custom field values keyed by field internal name.

For `number`, `currency`, and `percent` fields, an empty
string (`""`) clears the stored value — identical to
sending `null`. `0` and `"0"` store an actual zero.

For `checkbox` fields, send boolean `true` or `false`.
On read, a checked box serializes as the string `"Yes"`, an
explicitly unchecked one as `"No"`, and a box that was never
set as `null`.

Fields owned by an integration (for example
`swoogo_session_id`, `cvent_session_id`,
`visit_session_id`) are hydrated by the connector and
reject writes with `400` `FIELD_READ_ONLY`, naming the
field in `details.field`. Omit them from `custom_fields`.

Language variants to write using the same shape returned on reads.
Omit this key on update to leave existing translations unchanged.

400.description: Validation error — `name`, when present, must be a non-empty string

404.description: No sponsor with this id on this event. A record that exists but does not hold the sponsor role — a contact, or a group linked only as the other role — is also a `404` here; look it up on the endpoint for the role it holds.

409.description: Stale update — sponsor modified since last fetch

delete.description:
Soft-delete a sponsor. Can be restored with the restore endpoint. Requires the `write:sponsors` scope.

**This deletes the group, not just its sponsor role.** The path names the role you are calling under, but the record that gets soft-deleted is the underlying group, so:

* A group holding **both** roles loses its exhibitor role too. After
  this call it is absent from both searches and both `GET`s answer
  `404`.

* A group linked to **other events** is removed from those events as
  well — it is no longer returned by any event's sponsor or exhibitor
  search across the organization.

post.description:
Ask a question about one event in plain language and get an answer written for the
organizer. The answer is grounded in the event's program (sessions, speakers, exhibitors,
sponsors), session transcripts, the event's knowledge and pinned answers, and the
Sessionboard Help Center. `[n]` markers in `answer` point at `citations[]` entry `index` n;
citations are built from records, never from model text.

Read-only: nothing in the event changes and `actions` is always `[]`.

Requires the `read:ask` scope, granted **explicitly** — a legacy token with an empty scope
list does not get it. The token's event allow-list and the organization's AI features
switch apply.

**Slow.** An answer takes several seconds and can take up to 90; set your client timeout
to at least 90 seconds. If Sessionboard does not answer in time the API returns `504`.

To ask a follow-up in the same thread, send back the `conversation_id` from the previous
answer. A conversation continues only for the same token and user; any other
`conversation_id` starts a new conversation.

The API request log records the call with `question` redacted.

example.answer: Two sessions on Tuesday cover AI [1] [2].

citations.title: Panel: Where AI Helps and Where It Hurts

- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token does not hold `read:ask` (legacy tokens with no scopes included).
- `EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED` — the event is outside the token's event allow-list.
- `AI_DISABLED` — AI features are switched off for the organization.
- `FORBIDDEN` — Ask is switched off for this event (`details.reason: off`), AI features are off (`details.reason: ai_disabled`), or the organization is out of AI credits under enforcement (`details.reason: ai_credits`).

- `complete` — the email matched at least one record and erasure ran

- `no_records_found` — nothing in this organization matched the email.

`users_retained` — the compliance evidence of what the erasure actually
did. A user account shared with another organization is retained rather

Your organization's tasks, open ones first by due date. Filters combine.

- `assignee`: `me` (the API key's user), a user id, the email of a
  member of your organization, `none` (unassigned) or `any` (everyone).
- `due`: `overdue`, `today`, `upcoming` or `none` (no due date),
  judged in each task's time zone. `due_from` / `due_to` bound the due
  date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive).
- `record_type` + `record_id`: tasks linked to that record.

`counts` gives open, today, overdue, upcoming, no-date, milestone and
completed totals for the same filters, ignoring `status` and `due`.

Tasks are read as the API key's user: a key that belongs to no user
gets `400 USER_REQUIRED`. Needs `read:tasks`. Tasks are part of
Sessionboard Platform.

Creates a task and tells the assignee. Without `event_id` the task
belongs to the whole organization.

- **Assignee**: `assignee_email` or `assignee_id`; they must be a member
  of the organization, or a user on the task's event. The task's
  creator is the API key's user.
- **Dates**: `due_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and an optional `due_time`
  (`HH:mm`, 24-hour) in the event's time zone. For an organization task
  it is the assignee's time zone, else `America/New_York`. Without a
  time the task is due at 23:59 that day and `has_due_time` is `false`.
- **Records**: the records the task is about, each `{ type, id }`; the
  first is the primary. Every record must be in your organization,
  and in the task's event when the task has one.
- **Reminder**: with a due date and no `reminder`, the assignee is
  reminded at 09:00 on the due date (`9am`). Send `none` to skip it.

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description:
Expand records with additional data.

Possible values:
- `translated_fields` — includes the `translated_fields` array on records when the event has language variants configured.
- `subsession_details` — applies to session responses. Each subsession inside `parent.subsessions[]` is returned with full parent-session field parity (`status`, `custom_status`, `custom_fields`, `chairpersons`, `moderators`, `sponsors`, `exhibitors`, `tags`, `language`, `track`, `level`, `room`, `is_public`, `external_url`, `client_session_id`, `ceu_credits`, `capacity`, `source`) instead of the default minimal shape. Subsessions inherit `is_abstract`, `composition_status`, and optional `composition` from the parent. Not required when calling `GET /v1/event/{eventId}/sessions/{sessionId}` with a subsession UUID — that endpoint always returns the full shape at the top level.
- `linked_sources` — include sessions that are linked as composition sources (excluded from list/search results by default).
- `composition` — attach a full `composition` object with target and source details on each returned session. Recommended for single-session GET; use cautiously on broad searches.

A single value can be passed directly, and multiple values repeat
the parameter — all of these are accepted:
- `?expand=composition`
- `?expand=translated_fields&expand=composition`
- `?expand[]=translated_fields&expand[]=composition`

ListEventsExpand.name: expand
ListEventsExpand.description:
Extra collections on each event in `GET /v1/events`. Not the same enum
as session `Expand` (`translated_fields`, `composition`, …).

Repeat the parameter (`?expand=custom_fields&expand=integration_mappings`)
or comma-separate (`?expand=custom_fields,integration_mappings`).

- `custom_fields` — org-defined Event custom field values. Omitted from
  the payload when this expand is not requested. Present as `[]` when
  requested and the event has no values.
- `integration_mappings` — `{ name, source, external_event_id }` rows
  from conference `Integration_*_Event_Mappings` (via the union view).
  `source` uses underscores (`expo_platform`, not `expo-platform`).
  LiveBuzz / apps-engine campaign IDs are not included.

(`Session_Participants` + `Session_Roles`). Always returned on session
search and get (no expand flag). Includes custom program roles (for example
Author, Panelist) in addition to the legacy speaker/chairperson/moderator
junction tables. Legacy arrays above remain for backwards compatibility;
each legacy entry also includes `participant_role` when event roles are
configured. Contact profile fields (`photo_url`, `company_name`, `title`,
`address_country`, etc.) are hydrated from the contact record in the event's
default language without requiring expand.

language.description:
Assigned session language. Includes `id`, `event_id`, `name`, `order`,
`created_at`, and `updated_at` when set. Unassigned values are an
empty object `{}` on `POST` session search responses and `null` on
CRUD proxy responses (`GET` list, create, update, restore).

track.description:
Assigned session track. Includes `id`, `event_id`, `name`, `color`,
`order`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` when set. Unassigned values
are `{}` on `POST` session search and `null` on CRUD proxy responses.

level.description:
Assigned session level. Includes `id`, `name`, `order`, `created_at`,
and `updated_at` when set (no `event_id` on nested objects). Unassigned
values are `{}` on `POST` session search and `null` on CRUD proxy responses.

format.description:
Assigned session format. Nested session objects include only `id` and
`name` (not the full standalone `Format` schema).

room.description:
Assigned room when `location` is `room`. Includes `id`, `name`,
`order`, `capacity`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` when set. Omitted
when location is `external` or unset (`{}` on `POST` search, `null` on
CRUD proxy). `event_id` is not included on nested room objects.

subsessions.description:
Subsessions of this parent session. Each item defaults to the
minimal `Subsession` shape; pass `expand=subsession_details` to
receive the full `SubsessionDetailed` shape on every subsession
in the array. Composition fields (`is_abstract`,
`composition_status`, optional `composition`) are inherited from
the parent session.

Items are returned in the order set by the event admin
(`subsession_order`), falling back to subsession number and then
start time for subsessions that have never been reordered.

admin_url.description: Deep link to this entity in the Sessionboard admin UI.

SessionStatus.description:
A lightweight representation of a session's status, including
soft-deleted sessions. Parent rows additionally include a
`subsessions` array with the same minimal status-focused shape for
each child subsession. Subsession rows that appear in the flat list
return an empty `subsessions` array.

subsessions.description: Empty for subsession rows. Populated with `SubsessionStatus` items for parent rows, in the admin-defined order (`subsession_order`, falling back to subsession number and start time).

Contact.description: A contact (speaker, attendee, or organizational contact) in Sessionboard.

updated_at.description: When the contact last changed, from any source: an admin or portal edit, a sync, or a Public API write (create, update or bulk). Send it back as `updated_at` on `PUT /v1/event/{eventId}/contacts/{contactId}` or a bulk update for optimistic concurrency; the write returns the new value.

photo_url.description: URL of the contact's headshot. Images larger than 2 MB are delivered resized from this URL, scaled to fit within 2400 x 2400 pixels (a PNG may arrive as WebP for clients that accept it). The uploaded file is stored unchanged; for full-resolution originals use the bulk download tools in Sessionboard, such as **Download Headshots** (Contacts, More menu).

admin_url.description: Deep link to this entity in the Sessionboard admin UI.

examples.title: Professor of Computer Science

SessionSpeaker.description:
A contact embedded on a session (speaker, chairperson, moderator, or other
program role). Standard contact profile fields (`photo_url`, `company_name`,
`title`, `address_country`, etc.) are hydrated from the contact's module field
values in the event's default language. No expand is required for these fields;
use `expand=translated_fields` for other locales.

participant_role.description:
The event's configured program role for this participant (Sessions 2.0).
`name` and `slug` reflect the configured `Session_Roles` record (for example
Author, Panelist). `core_role` is the legacy junction category mapping only
(`speaker`, `chairperson`, `moderator`) and must not be used as the display
role label. Present on legacy `speakers`, `chairpersons`, and `moderators`
entries when the event has `Session_Roles` configured.

photo_url.description: URL of the contact's headshot. Images larger than 2 MB are delivered resized from this URL, scaled to fit within 2400 x 2400 pixels (a PNG may arrive as WebP for clients that accept it). The uploaded file is stored unchanged; for full-resolution originals use the bulk download tools in Sessionboard, such as **Download Headshots** (Contacts, More menu).

SessionAffiliation.description:
The person's company and job title for this session only, set by an
organizer on the session's participant list. A `null` value means
this session uses the contact's own `company_name` / `title`, so the
value to display is `session_affiliation.company ?? company_name` and
`session_affiliation.job_title ?? title`. Both keys are always present.

company.description: Company for this session, or `null` to use the contact's.

job_title.description: Job title for this session, or `null` to use the contact's.

ParticipantRole.description:
An event-configured session participant role (`Session_Roles`). Use `name` (or
`slug` for programmatic matching) as the participant's role label. `core_role`
is the legacy junction category only.

slug.description: Stable programmatic identifier for the role within the event.

core_role.description: Legacy junction category this role maps to for integrations.

allOf.description:
Sessions 2.0 participant row. Includes the same contact profile fields as
`SessionSpeaker`. `participant_role` is always present (sourced from
`Session_Roles`).

acceptance_status.description:
The participant's answer to their acceptance invitation. Present only
when the event has Participant Acceptance turned on
(`features.speaker_acceptance`).

acceptance_invite_sent_at.description:
When the acceptance invitation for this role was last sent, or `null`
if it has not been sent. Present only when the event has Participant
Acceptance turned on.

ParticipantRoleAssignment.description:
One role a participant holds on the event, with the sessions it holds
it on. Returned inside `Participant.roles`.

roleId.description:
The role's id — the value to pass in the `roleIds` filter and the
`id` returned by `GET /v1/event/{eventId}/participant-roles`.
`null` only for a standard role on an event whose roles have not
been created yet (see the endpoint description).

roleName.description: Display name of the role (singular), e.g. `Speaker`, `Panelist`.

slug.description: Stable programmatic identifier for the role within the event.

coreRole.description: The standard category the role maps to. Not a display label.

isCustom.description: `true` for a role the organizer added; `false` for Speaker, Chairperson and Moderator.

sessionIds.description: Ids of the sessions (including subsessions) on which the contact holds this role.

allOf.description:
A contact holding at least one session role on the event. Every
`Contact` field is present with the same values `POST /speakers`
returns; `roles` is appended after them.

roles.description:
Every role the contact holds on the event and the sessions it
holds each one on. Always the contact's complete set — not
narrowed by the request filters. Ordered by the role's
configured sort order.

EventParticipantRole.description:
A participant role configured on an event, as returned by
`GET /v1/event/{eventId}/participant-roles`.

id.description: Use as a `roleIds` filter value on `POST /v1/event/{eventId}/participants`.

slug.description: Stable programmatic identifier within the event.

core_role.description: The standard category the role maps to. Not a display label.

is_custom.description: `true` for a role the organizer added; `false` for the three standard roles.

sort_order.description: Position in the Sessions settings page; results are returned in this order.

Sponsor.description: A sponsor associated with an event.

address_coutnry.description: Country (note: field name contains a known typo preserved for backwards compatibility).

updated_at.description: When the sponsor last changed, from any source, including Public API creates, updates and bulk writes. Send it back as `updated_at` on an update for optimistic concurrency; the write returns the new value.

AccountContact.description: A contact associated with a sponsor or exhibitor account.

photo_url.description: URL of the contact's headshot. Images larger than 2 MB are delivered resized from this URL, scaled to fit within 2400 x 2400 pixels (a PNG may arrive as WebP for clients that accept it). The uploaded file is stored unchanged; for full-resolution originals use the bulk download tools in Sessionboard, such as **Download Headshots** (Contacts, More menu).

CustomFieldValue.description: A custom field value attached to a record.

value.description:
The formatted field value, or `null` when the field is empty.
Numeric field types (`number`, `currency`, `percent`, `quantity`,
`formula`) serialize a stored zero as its formatted value (for
example `"0"`) — `null` means the field has no value, not that
the value is zero.

`checkbox` fields serialize as the strings `"Yes"` (checked) and
`"No"` (explicitly unchecked); a checkbox that was never set is
`null`. Writes take boolean `true` / `false`.

`datetime` fields serialize as ISO 8601. On event custom fields
(`GET /v1/events?expand=custom_fields`) the value is event-local
time with the event's UTC offset (for example
`2026-08-15T09:00:00-03:00`), falling back to the raw UTC
instant (`2026-08-15T12:00:00.000Z`) when the event has no valid
timezone. On session, speaker, sponsor, and exhibitor custom
fields the value is the raw UTC instant.

`date` (date-only) fields serialize as `M-DD-YYYY`: month without
a leading zero, day with one, four-digit year (for example
`9-22-2026` for 22 September 2026, `3-04-2026` for 4 March 2026).
This is not ISO 8601; parse it with that exact pattern.

TranslatedField.description: A translated version of a field value.

TranslatedFieldWrite.description:
Write shape for `translated_fields` on create/update. Same identifying
keys as the read `TranslatedField` object; extra read-only properties
(`id`, `name`, `parent_field_id`, …) are ignored if sent.

Validation (applies before anything is written — an invalid entry fails
the whole request with `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR` and nothing is
partially saved):
- `translated_fields` must be an array of these objects.
- Every entry must include a non-empty `translated_language`.
- `translated_language` must be one of the event's enabled locales
  (the event default plus enabled language variants, e.g. `en_US`,
  `ar`). The error message lists the enabled locales.

translated_language.description:
Locale code for the language variant (for example `fr` or `ar`).
Must be enabled on the event; otherwise the request fails with `400`.

value.description: Value for that locale. Same type as the parent field.

Content.description:
A content attachment (file, document, or media) associated with a session.

**Approvals.** On events using Approvals (Early Access), a file can be held
back until it is approved and its release time has passed. The Session Files
endpoints still list a held file, so an integration knows it exists, but return
`url: null` until it is released. Publish only files whose `approval_status`
is `approved` or `not_required`. When a file you already published moves to
any other status, remove it from your destination.

url.description:
Download URL. `null` while Approvals holds the file back (see
`approval_status`), so nothing built on the API can publish it early.

type.description:
Organizer-facing file type, e.g. `presentation`, `handout`,
`poster`, or `holding_slide` for slides generated by Sessionboard.
Filterable with `?type=` on the list endpoint.

label.description: Display label shown on the session's Files tab, e.g. `Holding Slide`.

assigned_participant_id.description: Contact UUID of the session participant this file is assigned to.

content_slot_id.description:
The upload slot this file answers — see
`GET /v1/event/{eventId}/content-slots`. Present only while the
event uses upload slots; `null` for events on a single file
request, and for files uploaded before slots existed or outside
any slot.

approval_status.description:
Approval state, returned by the Session Files endpoints.
- `not_required`: not under an approval workflow (no workflow, workflow off, or uploaded before it was turned on).
- `pending`: waiting on a reviewer.
- `approved`: approved and released.
- `denied`: sent back to the uploader for changes.
- `superseded`: a newer version replaced it before it was decided.
- `embargoed`: approved (or not required) but held until a release time; see `embargo_until`.

Only `approved` and `not_required` files have a `url`.

embargo_until.description:
When an `embargoed` file is released (UTC). `null` when it is not
embargoed, or when it waits for its session to be scheduled (release
"when each file's session starts").

ContentSlot.description:
One file an event asks its speakers for (SB "upload slot"). Slots are
configured under Program → Settings → Files; `session_filters` and
role restrictions are internal and not exposed.

content_type.description: What kind of file the slot collects. Poster galleries read `poster` slots.

description.description: Instructions shown to speakers above the drop zone.

due_date.description: Deadline shown to speakers. `null` means no deadline.

due_date_extended.description: Later date the drop zone stays open until, if the organizer set one.

allowed_file_types.description:
Accepted type keys (`pdf`, `ppt`, `word`, `excel`, `image`, `png`,
`jpeg`, `gif`, `svg`, `video`, `mp4`, `audio`, `zip`, `csv`,
`text`). An empty array accepts any type.

required.description: Whether the slot counts as missing until a file is uploaded.

max_files.description: Maximum files per session; `null` means unlimited.

allow_after_deadline.description: Whether uploads are still accepted after the deadline.

order.description: Position in the list speakers see (0-based).

Tag.description:
An event taxonomy tag that can be applied to sessions.

The list, create, and update endpoints return `type`, `color`, and
`order`; tags nested inside a `Session` response and the search
endpoint (`POST /tags`) return the identifying fields only.

Track.description:
A session track (e.g., a conference track or topic area).

When nested inside a `Session` response, includes `event_id`. Standalone
metadata list and search endpoints (`GET`/`POST /tracks`) omit `event_id`
because the event is implicit from the URL.

Language.description:
A language configured for an event.

When nested inside a `Session` response, includes `event_id`. Standalone
metadata list and search endpoints (`GET`/`POST /languages`) omit
`event_id` because the event is implicit from the URL.

Format.description: A session format (e.g., Workshop, Panel, Keynote).

Level.description: A session difficulty level (e.g., Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced).

Room.description:
A room or venue location for sessions. When nested inside a `Session`
response, `room` is only populated when the session `location` is
`room` (not for external URLs).

capacity.description:
Maximum room capacity. Returned on nested session `room` objects and
standalone room list/search endpoints.

Subsession.description:
A subsession nested within a parent session. This is the default
minimal shape returned inside `parent.subsessions[]` when the
`subsession_details` expand value is not requested.

To receive the full parent-shape parity (`status`, `custom_status`,
`custom_fields`, `chairpersons`, `moderators`, `sponsors`,
`exhibitors`, `tags`, `language`, `track`, `level`, `room`, etc.),
pass `expand=subsession_details` on the GET or POST search request.
See the `SubsessionDetailed` schema.

`is_abstract`, `composition_status`, and optional `composition`
(when `expand=composition`) are inherited from the parent session.

Alternatively, call `GET /v1/event/{eventId}/sessions/{sessionId}`
with the subsession's UUID directly — the endpoint always returns the
full session shape at the top level.

friendly_id.description: Human-readable id formatted as `<event-prefix>-<parent-friendly-id>-<subsession-number>` (or `<event-prefix>-<subsession-friendly-id>` when the event has `show_subsession_friendly_id` enabled).

friendly_id_raw.description: Underlying numeric friendly id (the suffix of `friendly_id`).

parent_session_friendly_id.description: Human-readable friendly id of the parent session, e.g. `SESS-3370`.

parent_session_friendly_id_raw.description: Numeric friendly id of the parent session.

subsession_order.description: Admin-defined position among the parent session's subsessions; subsessions are returned in this order, falling back to subsession number and start time. `null` when the parent's subsessions have never been reordered.

translated_fields.description: Present only when `expand=translated_fields` is set and the event has language variants configured.

SubsessionDetailed.description:
Full-parity subsession returned inside `parent.subsessions[]` when the
`subsession_details` expand value is set on the request. The shape
mirrors `Session` (minus the recursive `subsessions` property, since
subsessions cannot be nested) and adds the parent-friendly-id fields
so callers can iterate the array and then call
`GET /v1/event/{eventId}/sessions/{sessionId}` with each subsession
id for the same shape at the top level.

`is_abstract`, `composition_status`, and optional `composition`
(when `expand=composition`) are inherited from the parent session.

subsession_order.description: Admin-defined position among the parent session's subsessions; subsessions are returned in this order, falling back to subsession number and start time. `null` when the parent's subsessions have never been reordered.

translated_fields.description: Present only when `expand=translated_fields` is set and the event has language variants configured.

language.description: Same shape as `Session.language` when assigned; `{}` when unassigned.

track.description: Same shape as `Session.track` when assigned; `{}` when unassigned.

level.description: Same shape as `Session.level` when assigned; `{}` when unassigned.

room.description:
Same shape as `Session.room` when `location` is `room`; `{}` when
location is external or unset.

SubsessionStatus.description: A lightweight representation of a subsession's status, included as part of the parent SessionStatus response.

subsession_order.description: Admin-defined position among the parent session's subsessions; subsessions are returned in this order, falling back to subsession number and start time. `null` when the parent's subsessions have never been reordered.

status.description:
The subsession's own approval status from the database. The API does
not inherit the parent session's status. May be null when the
subsession has no explicit status set.

SessionCustomStatus.description: A custom session status definition configured for an event.

status.description:
Approval state this custom label maps onto. Stored NOT NULL, so it
is always present on a status created through this API.

GDPRRequest.description: A GDPR data access or erasure request, and the record of what it did.

id.description: Identifier of the stored request. Quote this when evidencing a DSAR.

status.description:
Outcome of the request.

- `complete` — at least one record matched and was processed.
- `no_records_found` — nothing in this organization matched the
  email, so nothing was erased.
- `pending` — the request is stored but has not finished
  processing.

matching_user_exists.description: True when the email matched at least one record of any kind.

response.description: What the request matched and what happened to it. `people`, `users_scrubbed`, `users_retained` and `counts` are present on requests processed recently and absent on older records; an absent field means "not recorded", not "zero".

users.description: User accounts identified for this email.

people.description: Person records whose personal data was scrubbed in place.

users_scrubbed.description: User accounts whose personal data was de-identified.

users_retained.description: User accounts left intact because they still belong to another organization, with the reason recorded.

counts.description: Per-category totals for the arrays above.

Field.description: A field definition (standard or custom) for an event module.

contains_pii.description: Whether this field contains personally identifiable information (PII).

BulkOperations.description:
Request body for bulk create/update/delete operations.

Operations are applied in request order, each in its own transaction,
and `results[i]` describes `operations[i]`. A failed operation is
rolled back whole and does not stop the ones after it.

id.description: Entity ID. Required for `update` and `delete` actions.

data.description:
Entity-specific fields. Required for `create` and `update` actions.
Session create supports `is_abstract` (boolean, default false).
`is_abstract` cannot be changed on update.

`data` takes the same fields as the matching single-record
create/update endpoint, including `custom_fields` and
`translated_fields`. A `translated_fields` entry for a
language the event has not enabled fails that operation with
`400` and rolls it back — it is no longer accepted and
discarded.

`custom_fields` is honoured on the contacts, sessions,
exhibitors and sponsors bulk endpoints. An unknown
`internal_name`, a value of the wrong type, or a field owned
by an integration fails **that operation only** — the
operations around it in the same batch still commit.

**Exception — draft sessions.** `POST
/event/{eventId}/agenda-drafts/{draftId}/sessions/bulk` does
not accept `custom_fields`, and neither does its
single-record sibling. A draft session is a scheduling
placement of an existing session inside a draft agenda, not a
record of its own, so it has no custom fields to write. Set
custom fields on the underlying session through
`/event/{eventId}/sessions`.

BulkResponse.description: Response body for bulk operations, including per-item results.

batch_id.description: Unique identifier for this bulk batch.

results.description: Per-operation results in the same order as the request.

index.description: Zero-based index of the operation in the request array.

action.description: The action that was performed (create, update, delete).

status.description:
Whether this individual operation succeeded or failed.

Most bulk endpoints report `success` or `error`. The contacts
bulk endpoint instead names the outcome: `created`,
`associated` (the email already existed in the organization
and was linked to this event), `updated`, `deleted`, or
`error`. Treat anything other than `error` as a success.

id.description: The ID of the created or affected entity.

error.description:
Error details, present only when `status` is `error`.

An object with `code` and `message` on most bulk endpoints.
On the contacts bulk endpoint `error` is a plain string and
the code is returned alongside it as `error_code`; that
difference is longstanding and is kept so existing callers
reading the string keep working.

valid_options.description:
Present only when `code` is `TYPE_MISMATCH` on a
`dropdown` field: every value the field accepts,
one array entry per option, in the field's option
order. An option label can itself contain a comma
(`"Banana, Chocolate"`), so read this array rather
than splitting the list in `message`. Absent on
every other error.

example.message: Field 'product_type' value 'Banana' is not a valid option. Valid options: ["1", "Banana, Chocolate", "Blue, Green, Violet", "10"]

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code. Returned by the contacts bulk endpoint alongside the string `error`.

summary.description: Aggregate counts for the batch. This page previously named the object `stats`; every bulk endpoint has always returned it as `summary`.

total.description: Total number of operations in the batch.

succeeded.description: Number of operations that succeeded — every row whose `status` is not `error`, including the contacts bulk endpoint's `created`, `associated`, `updated` and `deleted`.

AgendaDraft.description: An agenda draft workspace for planning session schedule changes before committing them to the live event.

admin_url.description: Deep link to this entity in the Sessionboard admin UI.

DraftSession.description: A session placement within an agenda draft.

EventRule.description: A scheduling constraint or validation rule for an event.

Persona.description: An evaluation persona representing an attendee type for schedule evaluation.

ContentItem.description: Typed item inside a session or event content pack.

Transcription.description: Polymorphic transcription artifact. Fields vary by type.

s3_key.description: After complete, non-PCM uploads are stored as `.pcm` keys.

mp3_url.description: 6-hour presigned HTTPS URL for an MP3 sibling of the original PCM take. Null while the recording is in progress or if transcode has not succeeded yet. Download and store this file — do not hotlink it as a permanent CDN URL. Session PDFs and user-uploaded files stay on `/content` and `/files`.

mp3_expires_at.description: When `mp3_url` stops working. Request the recording again to refresh the URL.

size_bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes. Maximum 500 MB (524288000) for direct-to-storage upload. Use `POST .../files/upload` for files up to 50 MB without specifying size.

content_type.description: MIME type. Optional; inferred from the filename extension when omitted.

assigned_participant_id.description: Contact UUID of a session participant to assign this file to.

content_slot_id.description:
The [upload slot](/api-reference/session-files/list-upload-slots)
this file answers. Optional — API callers act as the organization,
so no slot deadline applies and a file may be attached without a
slot. When set, the slot must be active, apply to the session
(`GET .../content-slots?session_id=`), accept the file's declared
type and have room under its `max_files`; otherwise `400` names the
slot. The file's `type` is derived from the slot's `content_type`.
Ignored on events that still use a single file request.

url.description: Presigned S3 URL — PUT the file bytes here.

SharingForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED`: the token lacks `read:events` (reads) or `write:marketing` (writes).
- `EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED`: the event is outside the token's event allow-list.
- Otherwise the token's user cannot read (or edit) sharing on this webinar.

SharingNotAWebinar.description: The event is not a webinar.

TasksForbidden.description:
- `TASKS_PLATFORM_ONLY`: the organization uses a self-serve Sessionboard product; Tasks are part of Sessionboard Platform.
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED`: the key lacks `read:tasks` (reads) or `write:tasks` (writes). Legacy keys with no scopes can read but not write.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED`: the key is restricted to particular events; Tasks need a key without an event restriction.
- `FORBIDDEN`: the key's user can read this task but not change it (only the assignee, the creator, a follower or an admin can; only the creator or an admin can delete), or cannot use Tasks (reviewers and portal users).

value.message: Tasks are part of Sessionboard Platform.

LearningForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:learning` (reads) or `write:learning` (writes). Legacy tokens with no scopes cannot write.
- `FORBIDDEN` — Learning is not on for the organization, or the token's user lacks the Lessons permission.
